nativeGroups.readOrder: Retain the posted DWORD Event ID. When initialized, select its registry bucket by unsigned division remainder and walk collision links until the stored DWORD key equals it exactly. A found node is reference-retained before reserving the tag1 queue record. The record stores that same node pointer and posted ID together with the copied external allocation/carrier and the new playback serial. Missing Event or inactive engine returns zero; registration/queue allocation/completion and node lifetime remain conditions. No Event ID is a file key.

The admitted tag1 case reads the retained registered Event node from its queue record and walks that node's registered Action links. Each eligible, successfully allocated Action argument stores the current Action pointer, playback serial and retained external allocation/carrier from that same record before scheduling. Object-required actions can be skipped on missing object/data; allocation failure also skips the Action and continues the linked list. After traversal the Event node reference is decremented. This is native registered-list traversal, not a proof of its correspondence to authored array order or audible execution.

The reviewed normal Action execution body first calls the checked target lookup with this Action. A returned target primary object supplies the existing preparation and node-play address point; the Action argument retains the Event queue external allocation and serial into the same playback blob. Null lookup returns a local failure without node playback. Probability, preparation outcome, target subtype/address point and subsequent factory/provider success remain separate conditions.

Read the 14-byte AkBankSourceData prefix at the current cursor: plugin word, stream byte, source ID word, memory-count word and source-bits byte. Store the source ID twice in the parsed info region, the plugin separately. The codec-kind branch admits stream bytes0/1/2; other kinds and parameter blobs retain their own native branches. This native reader assumes readable input and is not a framing safety proof.

When the node type getter returns3, skip the serialized object-ID word and invoke the source-record reader. On result1 with no source-plugin parameter pointer, pass the separately read plugin word and copied16-byte info aggregate to the existing sourceSetInfo method at node+source displacement. That method stores the two source-ID words at source+0/+4 and the plugin argument at source+24; the already reviewed node-play wrapper addresses the same node source. NodeBase loading, host type dispatch, input bounds and live bank selection remain separate. The fifth Win64 argument is the bank-remainder selection byte, read from the stack after the original prologue and forwarded as the fourth base-loader argument. A nonzero byte can return source-load success while skipping authored node parameters; an omitted fifth argument is an invalid host probe ABI. Source-only witnesses do not prove the full bank parameter remainder.

Skip the serialized object ID and require equality between the stored16-bit Action type and constructed type. Read the target DWORD and following flag byte, normalize any nonzero flag to1, and pass the packed target/flag aggregate to address-point slot32. The checked normal Action target setter stores the target and replaces only its registry-selection bit. The remainder copies property/ranged bundles and calls the class parameter reader; its cursor safety and full per-class meaning are separate.

Read the stored Action target DWORD. Select one of two registry tables from its normalized target flag; unsigned remainder chooses a bucket, and collision links are traversed until exact DWORD equality. Retain the matching registry node and return its primary object at node-minus16, or null when absent. Lock contention and wait/signal branches remain native conditions; this does not establish current bank occurrence, node subtype or runtime target selection.

Complete unwindless leaf selected by the checked normal Action address point. Store target DWORD, then replace only bit6 of the Action target flags from the low bit of the packed flag byte; preserve every other flag bit. Its caller normalizes nonzero stored flags before this call. This is source-field transport, not runtime object ownership.

Read count and five-byte type/length headers from the supplied bank reader. HIRC type3 dispatches to the Action loader and type4 to the Event loader through the embedded table. This proves the format-family route, not an installed bank occurrence or live load order.

Obtain the HIRC Action body, exact-key lookup in the shared Action registry and retain an existing object. If absent, construct from the stored type, assign the stored Action ID and insert the object; read the stored fields for a newly inserted Action. An existing normal Play Action is reread only when its loaded-marker bit is absent. Bank owner storage retains the registry object. Registry mutation/locks, allocation and readable framing are conditions, not a same-bank identity proof.

Exact DWORD Event ID lookup in the shared Event registry. Existing entries retain their current list and skip authored-list reading. Only a newly inserted Event calls the record reader. Failed list loading decrements its reference, with destruction conditional on the resulting counter. The borrowed bank record is released and successful objects are retained by the supplied bank owner. Concurrent insertion/races and actual bank order are not inferred.
Allocate the Event object, initialize its registry header through the common constructor, install the Event address point and clear the Action-list head. Allocation failure returns null.

Skip the Event ID and read a high-chunk-first base128 count (continuation bit7), then little-endian Action IDs in stored order. Resolve/append each until the first non-success. A zero count returns success. The length argument is not consumed and no readable-buffer or continuation bound is established by this native reader.

Reject zero ID with status14; exact DWORD key lookup in the shared Action registry returns status15 when absent. Retain the resolved Action, clear its intrusive next pointer, set the Event head for the first resolved Action or previous-tail next for later ones, and replace the local tail. Successful unique resolved objects retain authored order. Duplicate Action IDs or reused objects across Event lists can overwrite links; no independent per-Event Action copy is allocated.

Initialize the common registry header, retain the supplied full Action type and clear intrusive next/property/range/target fields. Initial Action flags are set before the selected subtype installs its address point.

Complete unwindless dispatch leaf through its final tail jump. Mask the type argument to its category; category0x0400 tail-dispatches the reviewed normal Play constructor while preserving the full type argument. Other categories select other constructors or return null. No runtime subtype is inferred from Event names.

Complete common registry-header constructor leaf: clear the key, install its base address point and set the reference counter to one. It does not initialize next storage or establish allocation lifetime.

Complete normal Play per-class reader leaf. Read the curve byte and replace only the low five flag bits, read bank ID and bank type, advance the supplied cursor by nine bytes, set the loaded-marker bit and return success. Bank metadata is retained on the Action; it does not qualify its target registry lookup.

representations.externalDescriptor: Counted allocation: refcount/count header and copied fixed-size descriptors; a non-null UTF-16 path is separately copied.
representations.postQueueRecord: Tag1 post record retains copied allocation and auxiliary payload, with a post serial.
representations.pendingAction: Queue tag1 retains copied allocation into an action argument; action execution retains it into its node-play parameter blob.

evidenceBoundary.exact: Selected explicit GameAssembly.dll/global-metadata.dat/AkSoundEngine.dll inputs, named default-body claims, complete chained exception extents, per-window hashes, unwind identities, transport instruction bytes and tag1 dispatch-table bytes. Complete selected unwindless Action target-setter bytes are authenticated through their terminal RET and full contiguous instruction witnesses; they must remain outside exception extents. Complete bank Action factory leaf is authenticated through its terminal tail dispatch with contiguous instruction coverage, outside exception extents; HIRC type dispatch and registry constructors/loaders/readers have their own selected byte gates.
evidenceBoundary.direct: The selected native external-post path copies descriptors/path storage, forwards the owned allocation through a tagged event queue record, and the tag1 drain retains it into an action argument. The reviewed normal action address point calls an execution body which retains the allocation into its node-play parameter blob. A checked node address point carries that same parameter blob to a selector which conditionally clones a40-byte source, matches its stored word against descriptor rows, applies a reviewed source setter, forwards the selected pointer through a checked config address point to the existing source-owner factory, then addresses the embedded consumer interface. The checked bank source reader and node loader place the serialized source ID in the selector match word through the independently owned sourceSetInfo method, while retaining the plugin argument separately. The external selector uses the first cookie-matching usable descriptor in stored order and converts its raw argument into the replacement source argument using checked32-bit shift/increment instructions. The posted Event ID resolves by exact DWORD comparison in its registry bucket/collision chain before enqueueing. The retained registered node and external allocation are carried together in the same tag1 record; the drain walks that node's registered Action links and forwards the record's descriptor/serial to every eligible allocated Action argument, then decrements the Event node reference. The checked bank Action reader forwards its stored target DWORD and normalized target flag through the normal Action address-point setter. Normal Action execution calls the checked exact-key target lookup, which retains the matching registry node and returns its primary object for the existing preparation/node-play route. Bank HIRC dispatch binds Action and Event records to checked loaders. The Action category factory selects the normal constructor; newly inserted Events read their authored Action IDs and append resolved shared-registry Action objects to the queue-consumed linked list.
evidenceBoundary.conditional: Managed argument transport applies to the reviewed default body when its IFix replacement branch is not selected. The action-to-node argument edge requires selection of the reviewed action address point and successful preparation branch. The source-selection branch requires the original source argument high word, a matching descriptor, successful allocation/setter preparation, the reviewed node/config address points and the existing owner-factory branch. These are static conditional routes, not observations of a selected runtime instance. Bank-source loading requires the checked node-type result and successful reader branch with no source-plugin parameter data. Descriptor selection is conditional on readable allocation/row inputs. A selected wide-text route does not prove successful text allocation; it remains a void setter followed by local selector success. Event registry presence, initialized engine, completed record allocation/registration, eligible Action object branches and successful Action allocation are explicit conditions. New Event list order agrees with authored IDs only when every nonzero ID resolves to a distinct registered Action and no later link mutation occurs. Existing Event IDs bypass the new authored list; static reference-counter operations do not establish captured allocation generation/lifetime. Action type equality, chosen normal Action setter/execution address point, readable registry inputs and target presence are required. The two target namespaces are selected by the stored target flag; a matching ID alone neither establishes a Sound subtype nor selects a physical bank occurrence.
evidenceBoundary.structuralOnly: Native descriptor, queue and action fields have only their observed copy/retention roles; no complete SDK class layout is claimed.
evidenceBoundary.unresolved: Actual selected node/source/provider identity, live managed request-to-source ownership, allocation lifetime/address reuse, backing file identity, codec choice, lookup/open/decode success and audibility. The classic and source-consumer observer recipes remain unchanged; the optional source-bridge recipe does not admit runtime queue ownership.

evidenceBoundary.direct: A synchronous selector invocation can expose the carried allocation, original/clone pointers, selected descriptor row and wide-text argument before the admitted factory/constructor/consumer chain.
evidenceBoundary.conditional: Only the first descriptor is sampled. Count1 is required for one-row choice closure; multi-row selection remains outside this recipe. The wide setter has four additional stack inputs; only its first four register arguments and bounded source fields are captured.
evidenceBoundary.unresolved: Allocation creation/generation and reuse across asynchronous queuing, runtime selected node/config address point, complete descriptor choice outside count1, backing file identity, codec choice, decoded content and audibility.

bankSourceBinding.readOrder: The bank source ID becomes the selector match word through the source reader and existing info setter. The serialized plugin word becomes the source argument tested by the selector. Match words identify external slots, not physical media rows.

externalSourceSelection.readOrder: When the source argument masked high word is the external tag, a nonnull allocation is required and a40-byte clone is made. Scan descriptor rows in stored order. A matching cookie is usable first by nonzero selectionWord (with optional text), otherwise by nonnull wide text, otherwise by nonzero count plus nonnull memory. A matching unusable row does not block a later row. First usable row wins. The raw descriptor argument is shifted left and incremented in32-bit arithmetic before preparation. No matching usable row destroys/releases the clone and produces no selected source; clone allocation failure has a distinct local status. Other argument tags preserve the original source. The wide-text setter is void: its failed path allocation does not change selector success status.

evidenceBoundary.direct: Authored Action category/fields become registered Action objects; a newly inserted Event resolves authored Action IDs in stored order into the same intrusive list later walked by tag1 drain.
evidenceBoundary.conditional: Readable buffers, available locks, successful allocation/insertion, every required Action present, distinct resolved Action objects and no intervening link mutation. Existing Event IDs skip authored-list reading and reuse their current object. Registries are global exact-key namespaces, not physical-bank-qualified rows.
evidenceBoundary.unresolved: Actual bank load order, selected live registry generations, concurrent mutation, Event descriptor/source/file lifetime and decoder/output.
